decisions.reason: Changing the battery connector family, pitch, and pinout does not alter the established overcharge, overdischarge, or thermal-protection requirements.
The existing state already requires the battery NTC to connect through J_BAT; identifying NTC as one of the new connector's three pins leaves that monitoring requirement valid unchanged.
The connector specification changes, but the source does not change the battery connector's placement, orientation, spacing, mounting-hole clearance, or other mechanical-layout constraints.
The decision concerns the battery connector and does not alter the USB-C connector or its sourceability constraints.
The battery connector selection does not change how charge status is displayed or the GPIO and LED requirements.
The battery-interface connector change does not alter boost-converter enable control, pull-down resistance, or powered-load behavior.
The source decision does not change the requirement for TVS-based ESD protection.
The battery connector family and pinout are unrelated to the I2C cable length, clock speed, pull-up resistance, or pull-up location.
Selecting JST-PH for the battery interface does not revise the existing project-wide standards for component availability, sourcing checks, or compatible alternatives.
